findings.title: Conditional return within an enclosing consequence
findings.claim: The focus's conditional return and reply can leave mercy open while making the final confinement legible as a consequence that gathers force through repetition.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are عُدتُّمْ and عُدْنَا, the class named by لِلْكَافِرِينَ, and the final حَصِيرًا. At 44:15 a brief lifting of punishment precedes عائدون, while 8:19 places desisting beside returning; 6:28 imagines relapse after what was forbidden is exposed. The legacy walk also links the return pair to the 17:4-7 cycle. At the endpoint, 29:54 places Hell around the deniers, 18:53 supplies a no-route-away image, 17:13 is described as binding each person's record to the neck, and 17:97 names Hell as an abode whose fire is repeatedly intensified. These contacts turn the reply into a conditional recurrence and let confinement read as spatially enclosing and continually renewed. At 7:41, separate bed-and-cover imagery for Hell supplies a bounded surface analogy for the focus noun's woven-mat branch; the prison branch remains a distinct retaining-place sense. Finally, 6:122 pairs the denier class with darkness that cannot be left, and 11:9 pairs withdrawn mercy with كَفُور; these wider images let covering and ingratitude color, without replacing, the focus's denier category.
findings.reader_payoff: The verse's mercy, reciprocal return, and final enclosure can be perceived as one conditional movement: an opening remains, repeated action meets response, and the endpoint can be imagined as both surrounding and sustained. The woven surface, concealment, and ingratitude remain distinct contextual colors rather than competing definitions.
findings.containment: The wider passages are not asserted as quotations or determinants of 17:8, and they do not cancel its possible mercy or make return inevitable. The mat and covering contacts are analogical, not literal identifications; the woven mat and prison branches are not merged. Connection targets provide Arabic but no target morphology, and the 17:13 record detail comes through legacy-unbound reader support.

epistemic.reason: The focus carriers and several exact wider Arabic passages are supplied, but connection rows remain nominations without target morphology. The mat and covering contacts are analogical, while the 17:4-7 and 17:13 contextual details come from legacy-unbound reader supports.

findings.title: Hope alongside a path of repair
findings.claim: The focus's hopeful mercy clause can be heard alongside a wider pattern in which return through repentance remains an available route of repair.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is عَسَىٰ, which keeps the mercy clause in an open hope or expectation form. At 66:8 a call to sincere repentance precedes the matching عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ construction and an outcome of forgiveness and gardens. That separate act of turning meets the focus's hope wording and makes its open side legible as more than a pause before consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The mercy clause can remain open while a wider Quranic parallel gives that openness a practical shape through repentance and repair.
findings.containment: This does not make the focus's mercy certain or state repentance as its explicit condition. The wider passage does not gloss or determine 17:8, and the focus's return condition remains alongside this reading.

epistemic.reason: The wider Arabic is supplied, but its target morphology is not. The relation between the repentance act and the focus's hope is an interpretive contextual resonance.

findings.title: Confinement also reaches speech
findings.claim: The focus's confining role for Hell may carry a further, analogical effect of speech being held back in the wider scene of those gathered there.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is حَصِيرًا as the assigned confining condition of Hell. The wider 17:97 scene describes those gathered as blind, mute, and deaf before naming Hell as their abode. The place-and-inhabitant relation lets the branch of speech being held surface as an effect associated with the enclosure.
findings.reader_payoff: The final confinement can be perceived as reaching communication as well as movement, through the wider description of its inhabitants.
findings.containment: The focus predicate describes Hell's assigned role, not a mute person. This is a metonymic analogy from the inhabitants to their place, not a direct lexical gloss of حَصِيرًا or a claim that 17:8 itself describes the inhabitants as mute.

epistemic.reason: The exact wider Arabic and focus surface are supplied, but the transfer from the inhabitants' muteness to the confining place is an inferential, multi-step relation; target morphology is not supplied.

branch_activations.boundary: This remains an analogy about the wider scene's inhabitants, not a literal claim that Hell is speechless or that the focus directly says its occupants are mute.
